title: Servers, sudo, diffs and git
summary: Save root-owned files, compare files with vimdiff, and write good commit messages in vim.

steps.title: E45 and E212: you cannot write
body: You opened `/etc/nginx/nginx.conf` as yourself, edited for ten minutes, and `:w` says:
```text
E45: 'readonly' option is set (add ! to override)
"/etc/nginx/nginx.conf" E212: Can't open file for writing
Do **not** quit. Options:

1. **`:w !sudo tee % > /dev/null`** — pipe the buffer to `sudo tee`, which writes it to `%` (the current file name) as root. Then `:e!` to reload, or `:q!` because vim still thinks it is unsaved. (In neovim, `sudo` cannot prompt here; use option 2 or 3.)
2. **`:w /tmp/nginx.conf`** — save a copy, quit, then `sudo cp /tmp/nginx.conf /etc/nginx/nginx.conf`.
3. Next time, start with **`sudoedit /etc/nginx/nginx.conf`** (your own vim and vimrc, file written back as root on exit).
Always validate before reloading the service: `sudo nginx -t`, `sudo visudo -c`, `sshd -t`.
> **Practise:** open **Labs → Vim & nano trainer** and run this lesson's challenges until the keys come without thinking.

steps.prompt: Order the pieces of the command that saves the current buffer as root.
steps.explain: `:w !cmd` sends the buffer to a command's stdin; `tee %` writes it to the current file; `> /dev/null` hides tee's echo.

steps.prompt: Why does `:w !sudo tee %` work when `:w` failed?
options: vim itself still runs as you; it only hands the text to `tee`, which runs as root via sudo and writes the file
steps.explain: `%` expands to the file name; the writing process is `tee`, not vim.

steps.title: vimdiff
body: ```text
vimdiff old.conf new.conf      (also: vim -d, nvim -d, git difftool --tool=vimdiff)
]c  [c      next / previous change
do          diff obtain: pull the other side's version of this hunk into this window
dp          diff put: push this window's hunk into the other side
:diffupdate redraw the highlighting after edits
Each file opens in a vertical split; identical lines are folded away. It is the quickest way to compare a `.conf` with `.conf.dpkg-dist` after a package upgrade.

steps.prompt: Match the vimdiff key to its effect.
pairs: copy the other window's version of this hunk here
copy this hunk to the other window

steps.title: vim as git's editor
body: `git commit` without `-m` opens your editor on `.git/COMMIT_EDITMSG`:
```text
<- line 1: summary, about 50 characters, imperative
# Please enter the commit message for your changes. Lines starting
# with '#' will be ignored, and an empty message aborts the commit.
- Write the summary, a blank line, then the body. `:wq` commits.

- To **abort**, quit without a message: `:q!` (the file stays as git left it, so it has no message) or delete all lines and `:wq`. In an interactive rebase, `:cq` quits with an error code, which makes git stop.
- `git config --global core.editor "vim"` (or `nano`) sets the editor for git alone.

steps.prompt: Does git go ahead with the commit?

steps.title: What will Git record?
prompt: In `~/repo` a fix is staged. Its commit message is drafted in `~/COMMIT_DRAFT`, which still has a typo in the subject (`Fxi`) and Git's `#` help lines at the bottom.
1. Fix the typo with Vim from the command line (`vim -es -c '1s/.../.../' -c x ~/COMMIT_DRAFT`).
2. Commit the staged change with that file as the message, so that the recorded message has **no `#` lines** and no trailing blank lines.

Careful: `git commit -F file` does not strip `#` lines by default. When Git opens an editor it uses `--cleanup=strip`; with `-F` or `-m` it only tidies whitespace. Check what you recorded with `git log -1 --format=%B`. (A wrong commit is not a disaster: `git commit --amend --cleanup=strip -F ~/COMMIT_DRAFT` replaces it.)

checks.name: the commit message is exactly the cleaned draft
expectOutput: Totals were rounded per line, so a 3-line invoice could be off by
a cent. Round once, on the sum.
checks.fail: The newest commit's message is not the clean draft. Typo fixed? `#` lines stripped (`--cleanup=strip`)?

checks.name: the commit holds the invoice fix
checks.fail: The newest commit should change `invoice.py` only.

checks.name: there are two commits (nothing extra)
checks.fail: There should be exactly two commits. If you committed twice, `git reset --soft HEAD~1` undoes the last one and keeps it staged.

hints: `git commit -F ~/COMMIT_DRAFT` alone keeps the `#` lines. Add `--cleanup=strip`.
steps.explain: Git's cleanup modes: `strip` (drop `#` lines and surrounding blank lines; the default when an editor was used), `whitespace` (only blank lines and trailing spaces; the default for `-F` and `-m`), `verbatim`, and `scissors` (cut at the `>8` line that `git commit -v` adds). When Vim is Git's editor, an empty message, or `:cq` (quit with an error code), aborts the commit.
